clue.text: Tailor shuffled for bridge

indicators.note: shuffled says the letters of the word tailor are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: A tailor's cards are shuffled before a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffled' rearranges TAILOR. The Rialto is the famous bridge over the Grand Canal in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is a famous Venetian structure spanning the Grand Canal, an example of a bridge.

clue.text: Taken into care, what's the response ?

indicators.note: taken is read as taken apart, so the letters of into and care are mixed together

explanation.surface: A child put into local authority care, and how people respond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken into care' reads as one phrase, but 'Taken' rearranges INTO and CARE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a reply or answer to something, a response.

clue.text: Not that take-off here implies spicy entertainment

definitions.text: Not that take-off here implies spicy entertainment

parts.words: Not that take-off here implies spicy entertainment
parts.note: the place where aircraft leave the ground, whose name also suggests an undressing act, though no clothes come off there

explanation.surface: A warning that this kind of take-off is not the risqué sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as AIR STRIP it hints at a striptease, the 'spicy entertainment', but the take-off meant is a plane's.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is a cleared strip of ground where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: In some quarters men are held by principles

indicators.note: are held by means the men sit inside the word for principles

parts.note: tenets are principles

explanation.surface: In certain districts, men cling to their beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN goes into TENETS after its TENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenements are blocks of rented flats, living quarters.

clue.text: Kind of play of little interest to the palmist

definitions.text: Kind of play of little interest to the palmist

parts.words: Kind of play of little interest to the palmist
parts.note: a palm reader studies the inside of the hand, so its reverse side means nothing to them; that side also names a tennis stroke

explanation.surface: A style of drama that a fortune-teller finds dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' points at the stage, but it is a racket stroke played with the back of the hand facing forward, the side a palmist ignores.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke made with the back of the hand turned to the ball is a familiar kind of tennis shot.

clue.text: Jack detailed Nero to be captain of the host

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, the last letter of Nero cut off

explanation.surface: A sailor described the emperor Nero as an army leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'described closely' but means losing the tail. In the Bible Abner was captain of Saul's host, or army.
explanation.definitionFit: Abner commanded King Saul's army in the Old Testament, so led the host of Israel.

clue.text: Humble joints

parts.note: the leg joints one bends to the ground in a show of humility

explanation.surface: Modest little pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' tempts as cheap eating places, but these are the body's, which one bends to humble oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling, bending the leg hinges to the floor, is the classic gesture of submission and humility.

clue.text: Push off with a boast

parts.note: to vaunt is to boast

explanation.surface: Telling someone to leave while bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Push off' is the definition as an order: avaunt is an archaic cry of 'begone!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Avaunt is an old command to go away, like telling someone to clear off.

clue.text: Dandified Bob doubled into a squirrel's nest

indicators.note: into means the doubled letter goes within the nest

parts.note: a drey is the nest a squirrel builds

indicators.note: doubled means the letter for bob is written twice

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: A dapper man named Bob squeezed twice into a squirrel's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but is a shilling, s, in old British money; a drey is a squirrel's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy means smart and showy in clothes, as a dandy is.

clue.text: Parading in the top circle

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-class, top quality
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Showing off up in the highest tier of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is an old label for top quality, read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing views or clothes means showing them off publicly, a synonym for parading.

clue.text: If Edward dined here, you'd have to make it earlier

definitions.text: If Edward dined here, you'd have to make it earlier

parts.words: If Edward dined here, you'd have to make it earlier
parts.note: Edward is ED and dined is ATE; set them here after ANT and the whole means to give something an earlier date

explanation.surface: A host warns that a royal dinner guest means bringing the meal forward.
explanation.walkthrough: ED (Edward) and ATE (dined) end the word, and the whole means dating something earlier than it happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To antedate a document is to put an earlier date on it than the true one.

clue.text: Summon the peacocks

explanation.surface: Call together the vain birds.
explanation.walkthrough: A muster is the collective noun for a group of peacocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To muster troops is to call them up, and a flock of the showy birds is called a muster.

clue.text: Carry a thousand in one symbol

parts.note: to tote is to carry
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Lugging a thousand pounds inside one emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a carved emblem standing for a clan or spirit, a kind of symbol.

clue.text: Riots are a daily occurrence in the East

definitions.text: a daily occurrence in the East

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out every day in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the sun coming up each morning in the east, split as UP RISINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolts are risings, and the sun's appearance at dawn happens in the east every day.

clue.text: Head's a real tear-jerker !

explanation.surface: A boss whose stories make everyone cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onion' is old slang for the head; chopping one makes the eyes water.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang the head is called an onion, and the bulb makes cooks weep when sliced.

clue.text: Mavis has baby trouble

explanation.surface: A woman called Mavis is having problems with her infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mavis' looks like a woman's name but is an old word for the song thrush; thrush is also a yeast infection common in babies.
explanation.definitionFit: The mavis is a songbird of that family, and the fungal infection of infants' mouths shares the name.

clue.text: Frosty-sounding correspondence

indicators.note: sounding says the word for frosts is to be said out loud

parts.note: rimes are hoar frosts

explanation.surface: Chilly-toned letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but it is the matching of word endings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme is the correspondence of sound between word endings.

clue.text: It's harsh to create a scene about mounting 'dirt

indicators.note: about means the scrambled scene goes around the other piece
create means make a fuss, so the letters of scene are thrown into disorder
mounting in a down clue means the word dirt is read upwards

explanation.surface: Making a fuss over climbing dirt is grating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'create' rearranges SCENE to SENCE; 'mounting' turns DIRT into TRID; 'about' puts SENCE round it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridence is the quality of being loud and grating; 'It's harsh' describes that sound.

clue.text: Fleet Street clichés with a cutting edge

parts.note: Fleet Street was London's newspaper street, so it stands for a hack, a journalist
saws are trite sayings

explanation.surface: Newspaper platitudes that are sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was the home of London's newspapers; the definition describes the tools by their toothed blades.
explanation.definitionFit: These metal-cutting tools have a fine-toothed blade, so they come with a cutting edge.

clue.text: Administers punishment in odd snatches

indicators.note: odd says the letters of snatches come out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone is punished in short bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to discipline or correct someone by punishing them.

clue.text: Big victim of a fish-eater

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, meaning big
prey is a victim of a hunter

explanation.surface: A large casualty of something that feeds on fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish-eater' seems to be the predator of the victim, but it is the definition; OS (outsize) is a clothing label.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a hawk that dives to catch fish, its only food.

clue.text: Get to the water

explanation.surface: Make it to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: A reach is a straight stretch of river between bends.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place is to reach it, and a level stretch of a river is also so named.

clue.text: Notes dispatched, but not here

parts.note: A and B are musical notes
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: Messages went off, but nobody is around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing is away from the place, so not present.

clue.text: Hill worker has spirits in a cavity

parts.note: an ant is a worker in an anthill
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A labourer on a hill drinks liquor in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: An antrum is a body cavity, especially a sinus in the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy an antrum is a hollow chamber within bone, such as a sinus.

clue.text: Hair preparation makes changes in a blonde

indicators.note: makes changes says the letters of in a blonde are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A hair product transforms a fair-haired woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes changes in' looks like the product at work, but 'makes changes' rearranges IN A BLONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandoline is an old gummy dressing used to set and smooth hair.

clue.text: Turn to the lady, who else?

indicators.note: turn means the little word to is turned round

parts.note: her refers to a lady

explanation.surface: Turning to the woman and asking who else is there.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Who else' means who besides, a different person, so the word is a synonym of else.

clue.text: Clubs in Fetter Lane ?

parts.note: golf clubs with angled metal heads, and the shackles or fetters of a prisoner, as if found in the London street

explanation.surface: Gentlemen's clubs located on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Fetter Lane is a street in central London; the clubs are golf clubs, and fetters are shackles.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal-headed golf clubs share the name with chains and shackles used to fetter a prisoner.

clue.text: Put up by prize-fighters, noble fellows

explanation.surface: Boxers raise them, and aristocrats are them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up your dukes' means raise your fists to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fists are called dukes in slang, and dukes are the highest rank of the peerage.

clue.text: Oh Gareth, it's an aardvark !

indicators.note: it's an says the letters of Oh Gareth, when rearranged, become another word

explanation.surface: Someone tells Gareth he is looking at an aardvark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's an' is a mild anagram signal: the letters of OH GARETH become the other name of the African burrowing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is also known as the earth pig, a burrowing ant-eating mammal.

clue.text: Home, chum ? asks the lodger

parts.note: in means at home
a mate is a chum

explanation.surface: A tenant asks a friend whether they are going home.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate originally meant one who shares a house, a lodger or occupant.

clue.text: French husband in a job in the plant

indicators.note: in means the French husband sits within the word for a job

parts.note: a task is a job
mari is French for husband

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's husband is working in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is the definition: MARI goes into TASK after its TA.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery shrub of coastal and dry places, a plant.

clue.text: "He only does it to annoy Because he knows it --" (Carroll)

definitions.text: "He only does it to annoy Because he knows it --" (Carroll)

parts.words: "He only does it to annoy Because he knows it --" (Carroll)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing last word of the Duchess's lullaby in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A line from Lewis Carroll's verse about a sneezing baby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchess sings of beating her boy when he sneezes, because he only does it to provoke; the missing word completes the couplet.
explanation.definitionFit: The lullaby's word for what the sneezing does is annoys, provokes or needles, the sense filling the gap.
